about: Which runners take the pull request build's fallback (build-pr.yml, launcher-vps), which asks for this label alone because it needs nothing of the box. On the box only runner 2 carries it, so runner 1 is kept for main's builds: main's build is what traces the gate map the next pull requests pick their harnesses from (#3114, #3874), and when it waited behind pull request builds it took 49, 75 and 53 minutes from push to done instead of 18 (26 to 27 Oct 2026). Patrick's A on the report page, 27 Oct 2026 (q-4010-main-runner, #4010). Every box runner listed here must also be in records/build-runners.json, so the box's cap still holds (tests/test-2994-build-runners.ps1). offBox names One's runners (Install-Runner.ps1 -OffBox -Number n), which have their own cores and never carry thornswood-vps, so no box job reaches them (Patrick, 26 Oct 2026, #3860). A name listed there with no runner registered under it is named and changes nothing. Only thornswood-pr-one from 27 Oct 2026, 3:30 AM, until One's runners are on the Dev Drive (#4048; #4089, Patrick's A on q-3860-one-runners): with all five building, Defender (MsMpEng) was One's biggest process at 2.7 to 3.2 cores while the disk sat at 2% busy, every file read ran 50 to 100 times slower than on the box (the secret scan 5 min 23 s against seconds), and whole-gate builds hit the 40-minute job limit (#3860). thornswood-pr-one-2 to -5 go back on this list in the change after the Dev Drive steps are done. GitHub's runner labels follow this file on main: after a merge that changes it the Desk runs pwsh scripts/deploy/Set-BuildRunners.ps1, which starts github-admin.yml in the private ops repository, where the runners are registered (#3107, #4013). Install-Runner.ps1 registers a runner listed here with the label too, so a reinstall keeps it. Moot at the flip, when the box's and One's runners are disabled and GitHub's hosted runners take every build.
